spec.name: Contract Risk Clause Reviewer
spec.description: Analyzes contract text for five risk categories, produces a quote-verified structured review, and holds it pending until a human reviewer approves it.

contract_text.description: The full text of the contract to review (plain text or pasted document content).

contract_title.description: Optional human-readable name or identifier of the contract for labeling the review.

nodes.name: Validate contract text
nodes.description: Check the text is non-empty, long enough, and plausibly contract-like English; normalize whitespace.

nodes.name: Validity gate
nodes.description: Route to extraction if the text is a valid contract, otherwise to the error path.

nodes.name: Extract risky clauses
nodes.description: Scan the contract for the five risk categories and emit severity, verbatim quotes, locations, and plain-English explanations.

config.system: You are a meticulous contract analyst. You only report what is literally present in the supplied text. Quotes must be copied verbatim from the contract text (whitespace may be normalized). You describe risk in plain English for a non-lawyer; you never give legal advice or litigation strategy, and you never invent clauses or categories beyond the five listed.
config.prompt:
Analyze the contract text below for exactly these five risk categories and nothing else:
1. auto_renewal — automatic renewal/extension terms.
2. unlimited_liability — uncapped liability, indemnity, or damages exposure.
3. unilateral_changes — one-sided amendment rights, termination-for-convenience, or assignment without consent.
4. data_sharing — sharing/transfer of data with third parties, affiliates, or marketing partners.
5. non_compete — non-compete or non-solicit restrictions.

For each match, output:
- category: one of the five keys above.
- severity: "low", "medium", or "high", judged from the perspective of the party receiving the contract. Uncapped indemnity/liability = high; auto-renewal with a workable notice window = medium; narrow non-solicit = low.
- quote: the verbatim operative clause language from the contract text, trimmed to the relevant sentence(s), at most ~75 words. Do not paraphrase or fabricate.
- location: section number or heading if identifiable, otherwise "".
- explanation: plain English, under 100 words: what the clause does, who it favors, and the practical consequence. Avoid legal jargon; if a term of art is needed, define it in parentheses.

Reviewer context (may indicate which side the requester is on): {{input.reviewer_notes ?? "none provided"}}

CONTRACT TEXT:
{{nodes.validate_contract.output.cleaned_text}}

Return only findings for clauses actually present. If a category has no matching clause, simply omit it from the findings array.

nodes.name: Verify quotes & build coverage
nodes.description: Drop any finding whose quote is not verbatim in the contract text and build the five-category coverage summary.

nodes.name: Assemble draft review
nodes.description: Combine findings, coverage, and context into a draft review marked pending_approval.

nodes.name: Human review of draft
nodes.description: Pause for a human reviewer to approve the draft or reject it with comments.

config.title: Approve contract risk review
config.message: Draft risk review for: {{nodes.assemble_draft.output.draft.contract_title}}. Approve to mark it final, or reject with comments requesting corrections (e.g., quote adjustments).

nodes.name: Apply approval corrections
nodes.description: On approval, apply any comment-driven quote corrections and re-verify against the contract text; pass through unchanged if no comments.

config.system: You are a meticulous contract analyst. You only make the specific corrections requested in the reviewer comments. Quotes must remain verbatim excerpts of the supplied contract text. Never add new findings or categories.

nodes.name: Finalize review
nodes.description: Mark the review final and record the approval.

nodes.name: Revise rejected draft
nodes.description: On rejection, incorporate reviewer comments into a revised draft that stays pending_approval.

config.system: You are a meticulous contract analyst. You only revise the draft per the reviewer's comments. Quotes must remain verbatim excerpts of the supplied contract text. Never add new categories beyond the five allowed, and never give legal advice.

nodes.name: Invalid input error
nodes.description: Produce an error result instead of a partial review when validation fails.

nodes.name: Combine branches
nodes.description: Join the approved, rejected, and error branches so exactly one result continues.

nodes.name: Emit result
nodes.description: Shape the final response object from whichever branch ran.

taskSpec.goal: Produce a structured risk review of a contract that flags auto-renewal, unlimited liability, unilateral changes, data sharing, and non-compete clauses with quotes, severity ratings, and plain-English explanations, and hold the review in a pending state until a human reviewer approves it.

inputs.name: contract_text
inputs.description: The full text of the contract to review (plain text or pasted document content).
inputs.example: This Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one-year terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term...

inputs.name: contract_title
inputs.description: Optional human-readable name or identifier of the contract for labeling the review.
inputs.example: SaaS Master Services Agreement - Acme Corp

inputs.name: reviewer_notes
inputs.description: Optional context from the requester, e.g., which side of the contract they are on or specific concerns.
inputs.example: We are the vendor; watch out for broad data sharing with third parties.

outputs.name: risk_findings
outputs.description: List of detected risky clauses. Each item contains: category (one of auto_renewal, unlimited_liability, unilateral_changes, data_sharing, non_compete), severity (low/medium/high), quote (verbatim excerpt from the contract), explanation (plain-English summary of the risk), and location (section number/heading if identifiable).

outputs.name: review_status
outputs.description: One of 'pending_approval' (draft produced, awaiting human review) or 'final' (human approved).

outputs.name: approval_record
outputs.description: When final: the approving reviewer's name, timestamp, and any comments; null while pending.

outputs.name: coverage_summary
outputs.description: For each of the five categories: whether a clause was found, and if not, a note that none was detected.

steps: Receive contract_text (plus optional contract_title and reviewer_notes) and normalize whitespace/line breaks for analysis.

Scan the full text for clauses matching each of the five risk categories: auto-renewal, unlimited/uncapped liability, unilateral change rights (e.g., one-sided amendment or termination-for-convenience), data sharing/transfer to third parties, and non-compete/non-solicit restrictions.
For each match, extract a verbatim quote of the operative clause language (trim to the relevant sentence(s), max ~75 words) and record its section location if identifiable.
Assign a severity (low/medium/high) per finding based on exposure: e.g., uncapped indemnity = high; auto-renewal with a workable notice window = medium; narrow non-solicit = low.
Write a plain-English explanation for each finding: what the clause does, who it favors, and the practical consequence.
For any of the five categories with no match, record 'not detected' in the coverage_summary rather than omitting it.
Assemble risk_findings and coverage_summary into a draft review and set review_status to 'pending_approval'; present the draft to the human reviewer.

Wait for approval_decision input. If approve=true, set review_status to 'final', populate approval_record with reviewer name, timestamp, and comments, and apply any requested comment-driven quote corrections before finalizing.
If approve=false, incorporate reviewer comments as a revised draft and return to 'pending_approval'; never mark final without an explicit approval.
constraints: Never mark a review as 'final' without an explicit human approval_decision with approve=true.
Quotes must be verbatim excerpts from the provided contract_text; do not paraphrase or fabricate quoted language.
Only report findings in the five specified categories; do not invent additional risk categories in risk_findings.
Severity must be one of low/medium/high and every finding must include one.
If contract_text is empty, truncated, or appears to be non-contract text, return an error message instead of a partial review.
Explanations must be plain English (no legal jargon without a parenthetical definition) and under 100 words each.
Do not provide legal advice or recommendations to litigate; explanations describe risk, not legal strategy.
All five categories must appear in coverage_summary even when nothing was found.
successCriteria: Every item in risk_findings has all required fields: category from the allowed five, severity in low/medium/high, a verbatim quote that appears character-for-character (ignoring whitespace normalization) in contract_text, and a plain-English explanation.
coverage_summary accounts for all five categories, explicitly stating 'not detected' where no clause was found.
review_status is 'pending_approval' on initial output and only becomes 'final' after an approval_decision with approve=true is processed.
When final, approval_record contains the reviewer name and a timestamp.
No finding quotes text that does not exist in the supplied contract_text.
Each explanation is understandable to a non-lawyer and under 100 words.
assumptions: The five listed categories are exhaustive; no other risk categories are flagged in the primary findings list.
Severity is judged from the perspective of the party receiving the contract (the requester), defaulting to a balanced/vendor-neutral reading when reviewer_notes gives no side.
Contracts are provided as text at run time; no OCR, file parsing, or web lookup is needed.
The human approver is identified by whatever name/email they supply in approval_decision; no pre-configured approver list is enforced.
One approval round-trip is sufficient; rejections loop back for one revision at a time.
English-language contracts; non-English text triggers an error rather than translation.
clarifyingQuestions: Should approval be restricted to specific named approvers, or is any human approval_decision accepted?
Should findings also suggest redline language, or strictly identify and explain risks only?

This Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one-year terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term. 12. Limitation of Liability. IN NO EVENT SHALL PROVIDER'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY EXCEED THE FEES PAID IN THE PRIOR THREE (3) MONTHS. 14. Amendments. exampleInputs.reviewer_notes: We are the customer; concerned about the liability cap.

exampleInputs.contract_text: Employee agrees that for a period of two (2) years following termination of employment, Employee shall not directly or indirectly engage in any business competitive with Employer within any state in which Employer operates. Employee consents to the sharing of all performance data with Employer's affiliates and selected marketing partners.

This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues until terminated by either party for convenience upon thirty (30) days' written notice. Supplier may assign this Agreement or any rights hereunder without Customer consent.

plan.rationale: The core work is a single structured extraction over supplied text (no web, no lists of external items), followed by a mandatory human approval gate before the review can be marked final. A pipeline into human_approval, with a deterministic router on the approval result, satisfies the 'never final without explicit approval' constraint. Rejections loop back through one revision pass.

steps.purpose: Check contract_text is non-empty, long enough, and plausibly contract-like English (reject empty/truncated/non-contract input per constraints); normalize whitespace and emit cleaned text plus a validity flag and error message.
If validation failed, route to the error output path; otherwise continue to extraction.

Scan the normalized contract text for the five risk categories (auto_renewal, unlimited_liability, unilateral_changes, data_sharing, non_compete). For each match emit category, severity (low/medium/high), verbatim quote (trimmed to operative sentences, ~75 words max), location, and a plain-English explanation (<100 words, no unexplained jargon, no legal advice). Schema enforces the allowed categories and severity enum so downstream steps get typed fields.

Deterministically build coverage_summary covering all five categories: 'detected' with count where findings exist, 'not detected' otherwise; also verify each quote appears in the normalized contract text (whitespace-insensitive) and drop any that fail, guaranteeing verbatim quotes.
Combine risk_findings, coverage_summary, contract_title, and reviewer_notes into a draft review object with review_status set to 'pending_approval'.
Pause and present the draft review to a human reviewer with the contract context; reviewer approves or rejects (optionally with comments requesting quote corrections).
Branch deterministically on the approval result: approved vs rejected.

On approval with comments: apply any comment-driven quote corrections (e.g., extend a quote to include a carve-out), re-verifying quotes against the contract text; pass through unchanged if no comments.
Set review_status to 'final' and build approval_record with reviewer name, timestamp (from approval payload), and comments.
On rejection: incorporate reviewer comments as a revised draft (corrected quotes/explanations), keeping review_status 'pending_approval' for the next round-trip.
Join the approved, rejected, and error branches so exactly one result continues to the output.
Shape the final response object: risk_findings, review_status, approval_record, coverage_summary — or the error message when validation failed.

plan.output: risk_findings (array from extract_findings, quote-verified by build_coverage, possibly corrected by apply_corrections/revise_draft); review_status ('pending_approval' from assemble_draft/revise_draft, 'final' from finalize); approval_record (reviewer name, timestamp, comments from finalize; null while pending); coverage_summary (all five categories from build_coverage). On invalid input: an error message instead of a partial review.

risk_findings.quote: This Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one-year terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term.
risk_findings.explanation: The contract renews itself for another year unless you cancel in writing at least 60 days before the current term ends. This favors the provider, since missing the notice window locks you into another year of fees. Mark your calendar and set a reminder well before the deadline.

risk_findings.quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL PROVIDER'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY EXCEED THE FEES PAID IN THE PRIOR THREE (3) MONTHS.
risk_findings.explanation: The provider's total liability is capped at just three months of fees, no matter how much damage its failures cause you. This heavily favors the provider: if the service fails badly, your recovery is tiny compared to potential business losses. As the customer, you should push for a higher cap or carve-outs for serious breaches.

risk_findings.quote: Company may modify this Agreement at any time upon posting notice to its website.
risk_findings.explanation: The provider can change the contract whenever it wants, just by posting an update on its website — no negotiation or signature needed. This favors the provider entirely; terms you agreed to, including pricing or service levels, could shift without your explicit consent. Watch the provider's website and seek a clause requiring notice and your approval for changes.

risk_findings.quote: Employee agrees that for a period of two (2) years following termination of employment, Employee shall not directly or indirectly engage in any business competitive with Employer within any state in which Employer operates.
risk_findings.explanation: This stops the employee from working for competitors (or starting one) for two years after leaving, in every state where the employer does business. It favors the employer and is very broad — 'any business competitive' and 'any state' could cover a huge range of jobs and locations, seriously limiting future employment options.

risk_findings.quote: Employee consents to the sharing of all performance data with Employer's affiliates and selected marketing partners.

This favors the employer; the employee has no say in which partners receive the data or how it is used, and 'all performance data' is defined very broadly.

risk_findings.explanation: Either side can end the agreement at any time without giving a reason, as long as they provide 30 days' written notice. Because it applies to both parties, it is not entirely one-sided, but it means the job can end on a month's notice with no cause required, giving the employer flexibility to terminate quickly.

risk_findings.quote: The term of this Agreement shall be extended automatically unless Customer objects in writing.
risk_findings.explanation: The contract renews itself automatically unless you send written objection. This favors the vendor, since missing the objection step keeps the deal alive. The practical consequence is that you must track and send a written notice to avoid being locked into another term.

risk_findings.quote: Vendor's total liability shall be capped at an amount to be mutually agreed upon later, except that nothing herein limits Vendor's liability for its sole discretion.

risk_findings.quote: Vendor may unilaterally amend any provision, including pricing, without notice.
risk_findings.explanation: The vendor can change any term of the contract, including what you pay, at any time and without telling you. This entirely favors the vendor; you could face new prices or altered terms with no warning and no chance to object.

risk_findings.quote: Customer data may be shared with third parties as Vendor determines appropriate.
risk_findings.explanation: The vendor can share your data with outside parties whenever it decides it's appropriate, with no limits, purposes, or safeguards stated. This favors the vendor and exposes your information to uncontrolled third-party use.

risk_findings.quote: Customer shall not compete with Vendor in any market, forever.
risk_findings.explanation: You are barred from competing with the vendor in any market, with no time or geographic limit. This heavily favors the vendor and could block you from entire lines of business indefinitely.

meta.request: Review a contract text and list risky clauses (auto-renewal, unlimited liability, unilateral changes, data sharing, non-compete), each with severity, a quote of the clause, and a plain-English explanation. Require human approval before marking the review as final.

taskSpec.name: Contract Risk Clause Reviewer
taskSpec.summary: Analyzes contract text to identify risky clauses across five predefined categories, quoting each clause, rating its severity, and explaining it in plain English, then requires human approval before the review is marked final.
taskSpec.goal: Produce a structured risk review of a contract that flags auto-renewal, unlimited liability, unilateral changes, data sharing, and non-compete clauses with quotes, severity ratings, and plain-English explanations, and hold the review in a pending state until a human reviewer approves it.

inputs.name: contract_text
inputs.description: The full text of the contract to review (plain text or pasted document content).
inputs.example: This Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one-year terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term...

inputs.name: contract_title
inputs.description: Optional human-readable name or identifier of the contract for labeling the review.
inputs.example: SaaS Master Services Agreement - Acme Corp

inputs.name: reviewer_notes
inputs.description: Optional context from the requester, e.g., which side of the contract they are on or specific concerns.
inputs.example: We are the vendor; watch out for broad data sharing with third parties.

inputs.name: approval_decision
inputs.description: Human reviewer's decision on the draft review: approve (boolean), reviewer name, and optional comments. Provided after the draft review is produced.

example.comments: Liability quote should include the carve-out sentence.

outputs.name: risk_findings
outputs.description: List of detected risky clauses. Each item contains: category (one of auto_renewal, unlimited_liability, unilateral_changes, data_sharing, non_compete), severity (low/medium/high), quote (verbatim excerpt from the contract), explanation (plain-English summary of the risk), and location (section number/heading if identifiable).

outputs.name: review_status
outputs.description: One of 'pending_approval' (draft produced, awaiting human review) or 'final' (human approved).

outputs.name: approval_record
outputs.description: When final: the approving reviewer's name, timestamp, and any comments; null while pending.

outputs.name: coverage_summary
outputs.description: For each of the five categories: whether a clause was found, and if not, a note that none was detected.

steps: Receive contract_text (plus optional contract_title and reviewer_notes) and normalize whitespace/line breaks for analysis.

Scan the full text for clauses matching each of the five risk categories: auto-renewal, unlimited/uncapped liability, unilateral change rights (e.g., one-sided amendment or termination-for-convenience), data sharing/transfer to third parties, and non-compete/non-solicit restrictions.
For each match, extract a verbatim quote of the operative clause language (trim to the relevant sentence(s), max ~75 words) and record its section location if identifiable.
Assign a severity (low/medium/high) per finding based on exposure: e.g., uncapped indemnity = high; auto-renewal with a workable notice window = medium; narrow non-solicit = low.
Write a plain-English explanation for each finding: what the clause does, who it favors, and the practical consequence.
For any of the five categories with no match, record 'not detected' in the coverage_summary rather than omitting it.
Assemble risk_findings and coverage_summary into a draft review and set review_status to 'pending_approval'; present the draft to the human reviewer.

Wait for approval_decision input. If approve=true, set review_status to 'final', populate approval_record with reviewer name, timestamp, and comments, and apply any requested comment-driven quote corrections before finalizing.
If approve=false, incorporate reviewer comments as a revised draft and return to 'pending_approval'; never mark final without an explicit approval.
constraints: Never mark a review as 'final' without an explicit human approval_decision with approve=true.
Quotes must be verbatim excerpts from the provided contract_text; do not paraphrase or fabricate quoted language.
Only report findings in the five specified categories; do not invent additional risk categories in risk_findings.
Severity must be one of low/medium/high and every finding must include one.
If contract_text is empty, truncated, or appears to be non-contract text, return an error message instead of a partial review.
Explanations must be plain English (no legal jargon without a parenthetical definition) and under 100 words each.
Do not provide legal advice or recommendations to litigate; explanations describe risk, not legal strategy.
All five categories must appear in coverage_summary even when nothing was found.
successCriteria: Every item in risk_findings has all required fields: category from the allowed five, severity in low/medium/high, a verbatim quote that appears character-for-character (ignoring whitespace normalization) in contract_text, and a plain-English explanation.
coverage_summary accounts for all five categories, explicitly stating 'not detected' where no clause was found.
review_status is 'pending_approval' on initial output and only becomes 'final' after an approval_decision with approve=true is processed.
When final, approval_record contains the reviewer name and a timestamp.
No finding quotes text that does not exist in the supplied contract_text.
Each explanation is understandable to a non-lawyer and under 100 words.
assumptions: The five listed categories are exhaustive; no other risk categories are flagged in the primary findings list.
Severity is judged from the perspective of the party receiving the contract (the requester), defaulting to a balanced/vendor-neutral reading when reviewer_notes gives no side.
Contracts are provided as text at run time; no OCR, file parsing, or web lookup is needed.
The human approver is identified by whatever name/email they supply in approval_decision; no pre-configured approver list is enforced.
One approval round-trip is sufficient; rejections loop back for one revision at a time.
English-language contracts; non-English text triggers an error rather than translation.
clarifyingQuestions: Should approval be restricted to specific named approvers, or is any human approval_decision accepted?
Should findings also suggest redline language, or strictly identify and explain risks only?

plan.rationale: The core work is a single structured extraction over supplied text (no web, no lists of external items), followed by a mandatory human approval gate before the review can be marked final. A pipeline into human_approval, with a deterministic router on the approval result, satisfies the 'never final without explicit approval' constraint. Rejections loop back through one revision pass.

steps.purpose: Check contract_text is non-empty, long enough, and plausibly contract-like English (reject empty/truncated/non-contract input per constraints); normalize whitespace and emit cleaned text plus a validity flag and error message.
If validation failed, route to the error output path; otherwise continue to extraction.

Scan the normalized contract text for the five risk categories (auto_renewal, unlimited_liability, unilateral_changes, data_sharing, non_compete). For each match emit category, severity (low/medium/high), verbatim quote (trimmed to operative sentences, ~75 words max), location, and a plain-English explanation (<100 words, no unexplained jargon, no legal advice). Schema enforces the allowed categories and severity enum so downstream steps get typed fields.

Deterministically build coverage_summary covering all five categories: 'detected' with count where findings exist, 'not detected' otherwise; also verify each quote appears in the normalized contract text (whitespace-insensitive) and drop any that fail, guaranteeing verbatim quotes.
Combine risk_findings, coverage_summary, contract_title, and reviewer_notes into a draft review object with review_status set to 'pending_approval'.
Pause and present the draft review to a human reviewer with the contract context; reviewer approves or rejects (optionally with comments requesting quote corrections).
Branch deterministically on the approval result: approved vs rejected.

On approval with comments: apply any comment-driven quote corrections (e.g., extend a quote to include a carve-out), re-verifying quotes against the contract text; pass through unchanged if no comments.
Set review_status to 'final' and build approval_record with reviewer name, timestamp (from approval payload), and comments.
On rejection: incorporate reviewer comments as a revised draft (corrected quotes/explanations), keeping review_status 'pending_approval' for the next round-trip.
Join the approved, rejected, and error branches so exactly one result continues to the output.
Shape the final response object: risk_findings, review_status, approval_record, coverage_summary — or the error message when validation failed.

plan.output: risk_findings (array from extract_findings, quote-verified by build_coverage, possibly corrected by apply_corrections/revise_draft); review_status ('pending_approval' from assemble_draft/revise_draft, 'final' from finalize); approval_record (reviewer name, timestamp, comments from finalize; null while pending); coverage_summary (all five categories from build_coverage). On invalid input: an error message instead of a partial review.

risk_findings.quote: This Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one-year terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term.
risk_findings.explanation: The contract renews itself for another year unless you send written notice at least 60 days before the current term ends. This favors the provider, who keeps revenue by default. The practical consequence is that missing the notice deadline locks you into another full year of fees, so you must calendar the renewal date carefully.

risk_findings.quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL PROVIDER'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY EXCEED THE FEES PAID IN THE PRIOR THREE (3) MONTHS.
risk_findings.explanation: This clause caps the provider's total liability at just three months of fees, no matter how much harm its failure causes you. It strongly favors the provider. From your side as the customer, if the service fails badly — causing data loss, downtime, or business damage — your recovery is limited to a very small amount, leaving you to absorb most losses yourself.

risk_findings.quote: Company may modify this Agreement at any time upon posting notice to its website.
risk_findings.explanation: The provider can change the contract whenever it wants simply by posting an update on its website — no negotiation or signature from you required. This favors the provider. The practical consequence is that pricing, service terms, or other key terms could shift without your explicit agreement, and you would need to monitor their website to even know about it.
